fixes.fix: Explained "What do you know about Ravenhill Stadium (known as the Affidea Stadium for sponsorship rea"
fixes.text: 1) VERDICT: Ravenhill is a rugby stadium in Belfast, Northern Ireland. 2) WHY: It is the home ground for Ulster Rugby, a key venue in the Pro14/United Rugby Championship. 3) TRAPS: Do not confuse it with soccer venues like Windsor Park; the 'Affidea' name is a temporary sponsorship, not a permanent identity. 4) HOOK: Remember 'Ravenhill = Rugby in Belfast'. Exam trap: If asked about 'Kingspan Stadium', that was its previous name, not a different location.

fixes.fix: Explained "Ravenhill Stadium (known as the Affidea Stadium for sponsorship reasons from July _____, f"
fixes.text: VERDICT: 2025. WHY: Ravenhill Stadium, Belfast's rugby home, switched its naming rights sponsor to Affidea in July 2025, replacing Kingspan. TRAPS: Do not confuse this with the 2019 Kingspan deal or other Belfast venues. HOOK: Remember 'Affidea' starts with 'A' for '2025' (the fifth digit). Exam trap: Verify the month (July) and year (2025) precisely, as sponsorship deals change frequently.

fixes.fix: Explained "With the opening of a new stand for the _____ Heineken Cup quarter-final against Saracens "
fixes.text: VERDICT: The answer is 2014. WHY: The stadium expanded its capacity to 18,196 specifically to host the Heineken Cup quarter-final against Saracens on 5 April 2014. TRAPS: Do not confuse this with other rugby seasons; the date and opponent are the precise anchors. HOOK: Remember '5 April 2014' as the day the new stand opened, pushing capacity just under 18,200. Exam-day trap: Verify the year matches the specific match date, not just the general tournament era.
